title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: BM25 with Elasticsearch (Production-Scale Search)
summary: rank-bm25 is like a home kitchen blender — perfect for personal use, maybe up to a few thousand documents.

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy
sections.body: > `rank-bm25` is like a **home kitchen blender** — perfect for personal use, maybe up to a few thousand documents. **Elasticsearch** is like an **industrial food-processing machine** — handles millions of records, multiple servers, high concurrency, and built-in fault tolerance. Same BM25 algorithm inside, but engineered for factory scale.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body:
Elasticsearch (ES) is the world's most popular open-source search engine. It stores documents in JSON format, builds inverted indexes automatically, and uses BM25 as its **default scoring algorithm** (since version 5.0). It runs as a server, and you interact with it via a Python client or REST API.

When your document collection grows beyond a few thousand (to millions or billions), `rank-bm25` can no longer handle it in memory. Elasticsearch distributes the index across multiple machines, supports real-time updates, and serves thousands of queries per second.

sections.title: ③ Why Does This Matter?
sections.body: Every major company — Uber, Netflix, Wikipedia, GitHub — uses Elasticsearch or a similar system in production. Knowing how to configure and use ES with BM25 is a core production skill for any engineer building search or RAG systems at scale.

sections.title: ④ Step-by-Step Setup
sections.body:
**Step 1 — Start Elasticsearch with Docker (one command):**
```bash
docker run -d \
  --name elasticsearch \
  -p 9200:9200 \
  -e "discovery.type=single-node" \
  -e "xpack.security.enabled=false" \
  docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.11.0
```

**Step 2 — Verify it's running:**
```bash
curl http://localhost:9200
# Should see: {"name": "...", "version": {...}, "tagline": "You Know, for Search"}
```

**Step 3 — Install Python client:**
```bash
pip install elasticsearch
```

sections.title: ⑤ Beginner-Friendly Code Example
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Generator that yields bulk indexing actions
- Run a BM25 search query in Elasticsearch.
- Pretty-print Elasticsearch search results
- Ask Elasticsearch to show exactly HOW it computed the BM25 score.
- LESSON 15: BM25 with Elasticsearch — Production Scale Search
- Install: pip install elasticsearch
- Run ES: docker run -d --name elasticsearch -p 9200:9200
- Elasticsearch is the official Python client for Elasticsearch

**Defines:** `generate_bulk_actions()`, `es_search()`, `display_es_results()`, `es_explain_score()`, `es_filtered_search()`

```python
# ============================================================
# LESSON 15: BM25 with Elasticsearch — Production Scale Search
# Install: pip install elasticsearch
# Run ES:  docker run -d --name elasticsearch -p 9200:9200
#          -e "discovery.type=single-node"
#          -e "xpack.security.enabled=false"
#          docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.11.0
# ============================================================

from elasticsearch import Elasticsearch
# Elasticsearch is the official Python client for Elasticsearch
# It wraps all REST API calls in clean Python methods

import json
import time

# ── STEP 1: Connect to Elasticsearch ─────────────────────────────────

# Connect to local ES instance (started with Docker)
es = Elasticsearch("http://localhost:9200")

# Verify connection
try:
    info = es.info()
    print("=== Connected to Elasticsearch! ===")
    print(f"  Version: {info['version']['number']}")
    print(f"  Cluster: {info['cluster_name']}")
    print()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"❌ Could not connect to Elasticsearch: {e}")
    print("   Make sure Docker is running and ES container is started.")
    print("   Run: docker run -d --name elasticsearch -p 9200:9200 \\")
    print("        -e 'discovery.type=single-node' \\")
    print("        -e 'xpack.security.enabled=false' \\")
    print("        docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.11.0")
    exit(1)

# ── STEP 2: Define the Index with BM25 Settings ──────────────────────

# An ES "index" is like a database table for your documents.
# We configure k1 and b here — Elasticsearch lets you set them per index!

INDEX_NAME = "bm25_lesson"

# Delete index if it exists (for a clean start)
if es.indices.exists(index=INDEX_NAME):
    es.indices.delete(index=INDEX_NAME)
    print(f"Deleted existing index '{INDEX_NAME}'")

# Index settings: configure BM25 parameters
index_settings = {
    "settings": {
        "number_of_shards": 1,      # For small datasets, 1 shard is enough
        "number_of_replicas": 0,    # No replicas (single-node setup)
        "similarity": {
            # Define a custom BM25 scorer with our k1 and b values
            "custom_bm25": {
                "type": "BM25",
                "k1": 1.5,          # TF saturation parameter (default: 1.2 in ES)
                "b": 0.75,          # Length normalisation (default: 0.75)
                "discount_overlaps": True  # Don't count overlapping tokens
            }
        }
    },
    "mappings": {
        "properties": {
            # "content" field uses our custom BM25 similarity
            "content": {
                "type": "text",
                "similarity": "custom_bm25"  # Use our BM25 settings!
            },
            # "category" field for filtering
            "category": {
                "type": "keyword"
            },
            # "doc_id" for tracking
            "doc_id": {
                "type": "integer"
            }
        }
    }
}

# Create the index
es.indices.create(index=INDEX_NAME, body=index_settings)
print(f"✅ Created index '{INDEX_NAME}' with custom BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75)")
print()

# ── STEP 3: Prepare Our Documents ────────────────────────────────────

# Our document collection (expanded for a richer demo)
documents = [
    # (id, content, category)
    (0,  "Python is great for machine learning and data science", "python"),
    (1,  "Java is used for enterprise software development", "java"),
    (2,  "Python and Java are both popular programming languages", "general"),
    (3,  "Machine learning requires lots of data and computation", "ml"),
    (4,  "Data science uses Python for statistical analysis and modeling", "python"),
    (5,  "BM25 is a ranking function used in information retrieval", "search"),
    (6,  "Elasticsearch uses BM25 as its default scoring algorithm", "search"),
    (7,  "TF-IDF was the predecessor to BM25 and is simpler to understand", "search"),
    (8,  "Python scikit-learn provides TF-IDF and machine learning tools", "python"),
    (9,  "Hybrid search combines BM25 sparse retrieval with dense vectors", "search"),
    (10, "LangChain provides tools for building LLM-powered applications", "llm"),
    (11, "RAG stands for Retrieval Augmented Generation using LLMs", "llm"),
    (12, "Vector databases store embeddings for semantic similarity search", "search"),
    (13, "FAISS is a library for efficient nearest neighbour search", "search"),
    (14, "Neural networks are the foundation of modern deep learning", "ml"),
    (15, "Python decorators are a powerful metaprogramming feature", "python"),
    (16, "Java Spring Boot simplifies enterprise application development", "java"),
    (17, "Apache Kafka handles real-time data streaming at scale", "data"),
    (18, "PostgreSQL and MySQL are popular relational database systems", "data"),
    (19, "Docker containers package applications with all their dependencies", "devops"),
]

print(f"=== Document Collection ({len(documents)} documents) ===")
for doc_id, content, category in documents[:5]:
    print(f"  Doc {doc_id} [{category}]: '{content[:60]}...'")
print(f"  ... and {len(documents)-5} more")
print()

# ── STEP 4: Index Documents (Bulk Indexing) ───────────────────────────

# Option A: Index one by one (slow for large collections)
# es.index(index=INDEX_NAME, id=doc_id, body={...})

# Option B: Bulk indexing (FAST — sends all documents in one request)
from elasticsearch.helpers import bulk
# bulk() sends many documents at once — much faster than one-by-one

def generate_bulk_actions(documents, index_name):
    """Generator that yields bulk indexing actions"""
    for doc_id, content, category in documents:
        yield {
            "_index": index_name,          # Which index to put this in
            "_id": doc_id,                 # Document ID (optional but useful)
            "_source": {                   # The actual document data
                "doc_id": doc_id,
                "content": content,
                "category": category
            }
        }

# Execute bulk indexing
success_count, errors = bulk(
    es,
    generate_bulk_actions(documents, INDEX_NAME)
)
print(f"✅ Indexed {success_count} documents")
if errors:
    print(f"⚠️  {len(errors)} errors occurred")

# IMPORTANT: Refresh the index so documents are searchable immediately
# (Without this, newly indexed docs may not appear in search results!)
es.indices.refresh(index=INDEX_NAME)
print("✅ Index refreshed — documents are now searchable")
print()

# ── STEP 5: Basic BM25 Search ────────────────────────────────────────

def es_search(query, index_name, es_client, size=5):
    """
    Run a BM25 search query in Elasticsearch.
    
    'match' query = full-text BM25 search.
    ES tokenises the query and scores documents using BM25.
    """
    search_body = {
        "query": {
            "match": {
                # Search in the "content" field for this query text
                "content": {
                    "query": query,
                    # operator: "or" means any word can match (default)
                    # Use "and" to require ALL words to match
                    "operator": "or"
                }
            }
        },
        "size": size,   # How many results to return
        "_source": ["doc_id", "content", "category"]  # Which fields to return
    }

    response = es_client.search(index=index_name, body=search_body)
    return response

def display_es_results(query, response):
    """Pretty-print Elasticsearch search results"""
    hits = response["hits"]["hits"]
    total = response["hits"]["total"]["value"]

    print(f"🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print(f"   Total matching documents: {total}")
    print()

    if not hits:
        print("   No results found.")
        return

    for rank, hit in enumerate(hits, 1):
        doc_id   = hit["_source"]["doc_id"]
        content  = hit["_source"]["content"]
        category = hit["_source"]["category"]
        score    = hit["_score"]   # This is the BM25 score!
        bar      = "█" * int(score * 2)

        print(f"  Rank {rank}: [Doc {doc_id}] [{category}] Score={score:.4f} {bar}")
        print(f"            '{content}'")
    print()

# Test searches
response = es_search("python machine learning", INDEX_NAME, es)
display_es_results("python machine learning", response)

response = es_search("BM25 search ranking algorithm", INDEX_NAME, es)
display_es_results("BM25 search ranking algorithm", response)

response = es_search("enterprise software development Java", INDEX_NAME, es)
display_es_results("enterprise software development Java", response)

# ── STEP 6: See the BM25 Score Explanation ───────────────────────────

def es_explain_score(query, doc_id, index_name, es_client):
    """
    Ask Elasticsearch to show exactly HOW it computed the BM25 score.
    This is the most powerful debugging tool for understanding ES scoring.
    """
    explain_body = {
        "query": {
            "match": {
                "content": query
            }
        }
    }

    # explain() shows the formula breakdown for a specific document
    explanation = es_client.explain(
        index=index_name,
        id=doc_id,
        body=explain_body
    )
    return explanation

print("=== BM25 Score Explanation (Elasticsearch's formula breakdown) ===")
print("Query: 'python machine learning'  |  Document: Doc 0")
print()

try:
    explanation = es_explain_score("python machine learning", 0, INDEX_NAME, es)

    if explanation["matched"]:
        print(f"Document matched: ✅")
        print(f"Score: {explanation['explanation']['value']:.4f}")
        print()

        def print_explanation(node, indent=0):
            """Recursively print the score explanation tree"""
            prefix = "  " * indent
            value  = node.get("value", 0)
            desc   = node.get("description", "")
            print(f"{prefix}├─ {desc}")
            print(f"{prefix}│  value = {value:.6f}")
            for detail in node.get("details", []):
                print_explanation(detail, indent + 1)

        print_explanation(explanation["explanation"])
    else:
        print("Document did NOT match the query")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Note: explain() requires document to match. Error: {e}")

print()

# ── STEP 7: Advanced Queries — Filter + BM25 ──────────────────────────

print("=== Advanced: Filter by Category + BM25 Score ===")

def es_filtered_search(query, category_filter, index_name, es_client, size=5):
    """
    Combine a BM25 query with a category filter.
    'bool' query lets you combine multiple conditions.
    """
    search_body = {
        "query": {
            "bool": {
                # 'must': document MUST match this (contributes to score)
                "must": [
                    {"match": {"content": query}}
                ],
                # 'filter': document MUST satisfy this (does NOT affect score)
                "filter": [
                    {"term": {"category": category_filter}}
                ]
            }
        },
        "size": size,
        "_source": ["doc_id", "content", "category"]
    }

    return es_client.search(index=index_name, body=search_body)

# Search for "python" but ONLY in the "python" category
response = es_filtered_search("data analysis statistical", "python", INDEX_NAME, es)
display_es_results("data analysis statistical [category=python]", response)

# ── STEP 8: Multi-Match (Search Across Multiple Fields) ───────────────

print("=== Multi-Match Query (search multiple fields) ===")
# If documents had multiple text fields (title, body, tags),
# multi_match searches all of them with different weights

# For this example, we'll search content only but show the syntax
multi_match_body = {
    "query": {
        "multi_match": {
            "query": "machine learning python",
            "fields": [
                "content^2",    # "content" field counts DOUBLE (^2 = boost)
            ],
            "type": "best_fields"  # Score = best matching field's score
        }
    },
    "size": 5,
    "_source": ["doc_id", "content", "category"]
}

response = es.search(index=INDEX_NAME, body=multi_match_body)
display_es_results("multi_match: machine learning python", response)

# ── STEP 9: Get Index Statistics ──────────────────────────────────────

print("=== Index Statistics ===")
stats = es.indices.stats(index=INDEX_NAME)
doc_count = stats["indices"][INDEX_NAME]["total"]["docs"]["count"]
store_size = stats["indices"][INDEX_NAME]["total"]["store"]["size_in_bytes"]

print(f"  Documents indexed: {doc_count}")
print(f"  Index size on disk: {store_size} bytes ({store_size/1024:.1f} KB)")
print()

# Show current BM25 settings
settings = es.indices.get_settings(index=INDEX_NAME)
similarity = settings[INDEX_NAME]["settings"]["index"].get("similarity", {})
print(f"  BM25 settings: {json.dumps(similarity, indent=4)}")
print()

# ── STEP 10: Changing k1 and b (Requires Index Rebuild) ──────────────

print("=== Changing k1 and b for Different Domains ===")
print()
print("IMPORTANT: In Elasticsearch, k1 and b are set at INDEX CREATION TIME.")
print("To change them, you must:")
print("  1. Create a new index with new settings")
print("  2. Re-index all your documents into the new index")
print("  3. Switch your application to use the new index name")
print()

# Demonstrate by creating a second index with different k1/b
INDEX_NAME_V2 = "bm25_lesson_v2"

if es.indices.exists(index=INDEX_NAME_V2):
    es.indices.delete(index=INDEX_NAME_V2)

# New settings: b=0.0 (ignore document length) — good for short uniform docs
new_settings = {
    "settings": {
        "number_of_shards": 1,
        "number_of_replicas": 0,
        "similarity": {
            "custom_bm25": {
                "type": "BM25",
                "k1": 1.2,  # Lower saturation (good for titles/short text)
                "b": 0.0    # No length normalisation (all docs roughly same length)
            }
        }
    },
    "mappings": {
        "properties": {
            "content":  {"type": "text", "similarity": "custom_bm25"},
            "category": {"type": "keyword"},
            "doc_id":   {"type": "integer"}
        }
    }
}

es.indices.create(index=INDEX_NAME_V2, body=new_settings)
bulk(es, generate_bulk_actions(documents, INDEX_NAME_V2))
es.indices.refresh(index=INDEX_NAME_V2)
print(f"Created index '{INDEX_NAME_V2}' with k1=1.2, b=0.0")
print()

# Compare results between the two k1/b configurations
query = "python machine learning data"

response_v1 = es_search(query, INDEX_NAME, es, size=3)
response_v2 = es_search(query, INDEX_NAME_V2, es, size=3)

print(f"Query: '{query}'\n")
print(f"{'Rank':<5} | {'k1=1.5, b=0.75 (default)':<45} | {'k1=1.2, b=0.0 (no length norm)':<45}")
print("-" * 100)

hits_v1 = response_v1["hits"]["hits"]
hits_v2 = response_v2["hits"]["hits"]

for rank in range(min(3, len(hits_v1), len(hits_v2))):
    h1 = hits_v1[rank]
    h2 = hits_v2[rank]
    cell1 = f"[Doc {h1['_source']['doc_id']}] {h1['_source']['content'][:28]}... ({h1['_score']:.3f})"
    cell2 = f"[Doc {h2['_source']['doc_id']}] {h2['_source']['content'][:28]}... ({h2['_score']:.3f})"
    print(f"#{rank+1:<4} | {cell1:<45} | {cell2:<45}")

print()

# ── STEP 11: Cleanup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

print("=== Cleanup ===")
es.indices.delete(index=INDEX_NAME)
es.indices.delete(index=INDEX_NAME_V2)
print(f"Deleted indices '{INDEX_NAME}' and '{INDEX_NAME_V2}'")
print()
print("Lesson 15 complete! ✅")
```

sections.title: ⑥ Common Beginner Mistakes (Lesson 15)
sections.body:
❌ **Mistake 1:** Forgetting to refresh the index after bulk indexing — documents don't appear in results
✅ **Fix:** Always call `es.indices.refresh(index=INDEX_NAME)` after bulk indexing in development

❌ **Mistake 2:** Setting k1 and b AFTER creating the index — they're immutable post-creation
✅ **Fix:** Define similarity settings in the index creation body; rebuild the index to change them

❌ **Mistake 3:** Using `query` instead of `filter` for category filtering — costs score computation unnecessarily
✅ **Fix:** Put non-scoring conditions in `filter` context (faster, cached by ES)

❌ **Mistake 4:** Indexing documents one-by-one instead of bulk indexing — extremely slow
✅ **Fix:** Always use `elasticsearch.helpers.bulk()` for loading large document collections

❌ **Mistake 5:** Not setting `"discovery.type=single-node"` — ES waits for other nodes that never come
✅ **Fix:** For local/dev setup always include `discovery.type=single-node` in Docker env vars

sections.title: ⑦ Quick Recap (Lesson 15)
sections.body:
- 🔍 Elasticsearch uses **BM25 by default** — it's the `match` query scorer
- ⚙️ Set **k1 and b** in index creation settings under `"similarity"` configuration
- 📦 Use **`bulk()`** from `elasticsearch.helpers` — never index one document at a time
- 🔄 Always **refresh the index** after bulk operations in development
- 🔬 Use **`explain=True`** / `es.explain()` to see exactly how BM25 computed each score

sections.title: ⑧ Visual Explanation (Lesson 15)
sections.body:
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║        ELASTICSEARCH + BM25 — COMPLETE ARCHITECTURE GUIDE            ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

 SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
 ════════════════════

 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Your Python Application                    │
 │                                                                │
 │   from elasticsearch import Elasticsearch                      │
 │   es = Elasticsearch("http://localhost:9200")                  │
 └────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │  HTTP REST API
                              │  (JSON over HTTP)
                              ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                    Elasticsearch Node                          │
 │                                                                │
 │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
 │  │                  Index: "bm25_lesson"                    │ │
 │  │                                                          │ │
 │  │  Settings:                    Mapping:                   │ │
 │  │  k1 = 1.5  ──────┐           content: text + BM25      │ │
 │  │  b  = 0.75 ──────┤           category: keyword          │ │
 │  │                   │           doc_id: integer            │ │
 │  │                   ▼                                      │ │
 │  │           ┌──────────────┐                               │ │
 │  │           │ BM25 Scorer  │                               │ │
 │  │           │              │                               │ │
 │  │           │  IDF(term)   │                               │ │
 │  │           │  × TF_comp   │                               │ │
 │  │           │  (k1, b,     │                               │ │
 │  │           │   avgdl)     │                               │ │
 │  │           └──────────────┘                               │ │
 │  │                   │                                      │ │
 │  │           ┌──────────────┐                               │ │
 │  │           │Inverted Index│                               │ │
 │  │           │              │                               │ │
 │  │           │"python"→[0,2]│                               │ │
 │  │           │"java" →[1,2] │                               │ │
 │  │           │  ...         │                               │ │
 │  │           └──────────────┘                               │ │
 │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 THE QUERY LIFECYCLE IN ELASTICSEARCH
 ══════════════════════════════════════

 1. You send: POST /bm25_lesson/_search
              {"query": {"match": {"content": "python machine learning"}}}

 2. ES tokenises query: ["python", "machine", "learning"]

 3. For each token, ES looks up the inverted index:
    "python"   → [Doc0, Doc2, Doc4, Doc8, Doc15]
    "machine"  → [Doc0, Doc3, Doc8, Doc14]
    "learning" → [Doc0, Doc3, Doc8, Doc14]

 4. ES computes BM25 score for each matching document
    using YOUR custom k1=1.5, b=0.75

 5. ES sorts by score, returns top-N

 6. You receive: {"hits": [{"_score": 3.67, "_source": {...}}, ...]}

 QUERY TYPES CHEAT SHEET
 ════════════════════════

 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  Query Type    │  Use When                │  Affects Score?     │
 │────────────────│──────────────────────────│─────────────────────│
 │  match         │  Full-text BM25 search   │  YES ✅              │
 │  term          │  Exact value match       │  YES ✅              │
 │  bool.must     │  Required + scored       │  YES ✅              │
 │  bool.filter   │  Required + NOT scored   │  NO ⚡ (faster)     │
 │  bool.should   │  Optional (boost score)  │  YES ✅              │
 │  multi_match   │  Search multiple fields  │  YES ✅              │
 │  match_phrase  │  Exact phrase match      │  YES ✅              │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 BM25 SCORE EXPLANATION TREE (from explain API)
 ═══════════════════════════════════════════════

 Total score: 3.672
 └── sum of per-term scores:
     ├── "python" contribution: 1.224
     │   ├── IDF = 0.539    (appears in 3/20 docs → medium rarity)
     │   └── TF  = 0.958    (appears 1× in this 9-word doc)
     │         └── formula: f×(k1+1) / (f + k1×length_factor)
     │                       1×2.5   / (1  + 1.5×1.073) = 0.958
     ├── "machine" contribution: 1.199
     │   ├── IDF = 0.875    (appears in 2/20 docs → higher rarity)
     │   └── TF  = 0.958
     └── "learning" contribution: 1.249
         ├── IDF = 0.875
         └── TF  = 0.958

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Quick Reference — All Libraries
sections.body:
```bash
# Core BM25
pip install rank-bm25

# Text preprocessing
pip install nltk spacy
python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
python -m nltk.downloader stopwords punkt

# TF-IDF baseline
pip install scikit-learn

# Dense retrieval
pip install sentence-transformers faiss-cpu

# LangChain RAG
pip install langchain langchain-community

# Production search
pip install elasticsearch
docker run -d --name elasticsearch -p 9200:9200 \
  -e "discovery.type=single-node" \
  -e "xpack.security.enabled=false" \
  docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.11.0

# Visualisation
pip install matplotlib numpy
```

> 🎉 **Congratulations Veera!** You've gone from "what is a search engine?" all the way to building production-scale hybrid BM25 + vector search pipelines. You now understand every symbol in the BM25 formula, can implement it from scratch, tune its parameters, and deploy it at scale. That's an enormous achievement!
